pages.text: Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum | National Geographic 1:00 Artist's impression of the Ichthyosaurus ILLUSTRATION BY JOSCHUA KNÜPPE Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum The paleontologist who made the discovery was originally at the museum to study a fossil that resembles the Loch Ness monster. By Sarah Gibbens Published August 28, 2017 • 4 min read Sven Sachs, a paleontologist from the Bielefeld Natural History Museum in Germany, was at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover to study an ancient sea reptile when one of the museum's display fossils caught his eye. The specimen had originally been unearthed in the mid-1990s in Somerset, England, but it had remained largely unstudied since. Sachs suspected it was an Ichthyosaurus. Commonly mistaken for a dinosaur, the species was more like a "sea dragon" marine reptile that had a long, flexible body and may have swum like eels. "I found it very extraordinary," said Sachs. "[It was] way bigger than any specimen I had examined." He explained the specimen had previously been labeled as a smaller species within the Ichthyosaurus group. Sachs reached out to Ichthyosaurus expert Dean Lomax from the University of Manchester, and in early 2017 they examined the specimen together, finding it to be a specimen of the species Ichthyosaurus somersetensis . Skeleton of Ichthyosaurus . Photograph by Dean Lomax Their findings, published in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , describe the largest known specimen of its kind. Credit: M. King/NIST Even if you’ve never heard of “light caustics,” you’ve probably seen them. They’re the ethereal patterns of light that coat the bottoms of swimming pools and break up the shadows of glass. Anywhere light is bent or reflected by a curved surface, caustics can appear. This trick of the light is turning out to be an important tool for 3D-printing metal, a process in which high-powered lasers melt metal powder one layer at a time. NIST scientists have found that caustic reflections from those lasers contain clues about the metal’s microscopic shape. This research will give us never-before-seen, real-time insights into metal 3D printing. What’s Metal 3D Printing? pages.text: Learn about the United States' founding documents | USAGov Skip to main content Learn about the United States' founding documents The Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and Bill of Rights, known together as the Charters of Freedom, established the government’s structure and continue to secure the rights of American citizens. Declaration of Independence The Declaration of Independence proclaimed that the American colonies were separating from British rule, and detailed the reasons. On July 4, 1776, Congress voted to accept the Declaration of Independence, marking July 4 as Independence Day. Thomas Jefferson, the principal author, drafted the document in 17 days. U.S. Constitution The Constitution of the United States set up the foundation of the U.S. government, including its purpose and structure. The Constitutional Convention adopted the Constitution on September 17, 1787. Bill of Rights The Bill of Rights is the first 10 amendments (changes) to the U.S. Constitution. It guarantees greater protection for individual freedoms and lists specific limits on government power. The Constitution has 27 amendments in all. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. Los Texmaniacs: Tiny Desk Concert October 8, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Zayrha Rodriguez/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Los Texmaniacs ' music is a living history lesson. The conjunto sound is driven by the button accordion, a mid-19th century instrument that made its way to the U.S.-Mexico border by way of German, Czech and Polish immigrants. But this music is also just perfect for twirling on the dance floor to songs about true love, heartbreak, folk heroes and reflections on life. First of all, it was the final production of our sixth annual El Tiny series. This was a very emotional moment for a lot of reasons. People really love Los Tigres del Norte, to the point that playing their albums feels like sitting with family. And if you’ve seen the introduction I gave the band just before they played at the desk you can see that I wasn’t embarrassed to get emotional when I talked about what the band means to me. That emotional intro led to some changes in our process and format that resulted in a huge response from the audience that went viral. The result was a messy moment behind the scenes here at NPR and more than a little confusion for a lot of you. This week’s episode looks back at last week. First we want to share with you, directly from us, an explanation of what happened. But mostly we want to put the spotlight back on the band and their music because for decades they have been bringing out the kind emotions that got this whole thing started. Give it a listen and enjoy the music. Again. - Felix This podcast episode was produced by Noah Caldwell and edited by Jacob Ganz and Otis Hart. Suraya Mohamed is the executive producer of NPR Music. They provide inspiration for advances in technology, they support cave communities, and they even help bring us some of our most tasty treats! Bats act as natural gardeners, helping grow many of the foods we eat through insect control, pollination, and seed dispersal. Insect Control Foods that benefit from bat insect control. NPS Bats that eat insects are called "insectivorous." They feast on insects each night, adding up to more than $3.7 billion worth of pest control each year in the U.S. When bats are around to eat insects, there are fewer insect pests causing damage to crops, and farmers don't have to invest as much in pesticides. Imagine eating 200 quarter-pound burgers -- that's how much a bat eats in insects in one night! pages.description: The man, a Mexican firefighter, looked "nervous" as he tried to leave Cologne Airport, officials say.
pages.text: Man with venomous snakes and lizards stopped at German airport Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Man with suitcase full of snakes stopped at German airport 15 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Paulin Kola German Customs Not all the the snakes and lizards were alive, officials said A man has been stopped at Cologne Bonn Airport in Germany after trying to smuggle in more than 90 lizards and venomous snakes. Customs officials said the 45-year-old Mexican firefighter had looked "conspicuously nervous" as he tried to go through the green - nothing to declare - exit at the airport. They conducted a drugs test on the man - which came back positive for cocaine - before proceeding to check his suitcase. They did not find any drugs, but vipers, rattlesnakes and other species of snakes and lizards, including iguanas, hidden in shampoo and cream bottles, plastic containers and balls of socks. "My colleagues at the airport are used to a lot when it comes to souvenirs in suitcases, but we've never had 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards from Mexico before," said Jens Ahland, spokesman for the Cologne Customs office. Some were being kept "in inhumane conditions", Ahland said. Others had died during the journey from Mexico City via Istanbul. The man, who has not been named, told officers that he had brought the animals back as a favour for a Brazilian acquaintance. He was denied entry to Germany and flown back to Istanbul.
